front_matter.preface: Tangkhul-English, Hindi Dictionary by Dr. S. Arokianathan and Dr. Rekha Sharma, published by the Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore (CIIL Dictionary Series, 1995, 140 pages, ISBN 81-7342-028-9). Provides systematic lexicographical descriptions of Tangkhul root morphemes, compounds, word classes, English definitions, and Hindi equivalents.

chapters.summary: Vowel length, aspirated plosives, and trilingual lexicographical entry conventions.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Lexicographical Format: Headword [Part of Speech] English Definition / Hindi Equivalent. Minimal vowel length contrasts: 'sa' [v] to do / करना vs 'sā' [n] animal, meat / पशु, माँस. 'sha' [v] to hear / सुनना vs 'shā' [num] hundred / सौ. Infinitive prefix ka- precedes verbal roots: ka-sa, ka-thei, ka-shak.
chapters.english_translation: Conventions: Headwords are alphabetized according to Roman script order. Phonemic vowel length (macron) is strictly distinguished. Trilingual definitions provide immediate cross-linguistic equivalents in English and Hindi.

pages.tangkhul_content: Tangkhul tui kala ngashan kashak lairiksa. Thot kachungwui vang mashunseru.
pages.english_translation: Preserved for future generations to uphold and celebrate the Tangkhul language.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: Lexicographical Format: Headword [Part of Speech] English Definition / Hindi Equivalent. Minimal vowel length contrasts: 'sa' [v] to do / करना vs 'sā' [n] animal, meat / पशु, माँस. 'sha' [v] to hear / सुनना vs 'shā' [num] hundred / सौ. Infinitive prefix ka- precedes verbal roots: ka-sa, ka-thei, ka-shak.
excerpts.translation_en: Conventions: Headwords are alphabetized according to Roman script order. Phonemic vowel length (macron) is strictly distinguished. Trilingual definitions provide immediate cross-linguistic equivalents in English and Hindi.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Nominal Vocabulary: Body Parts, Kinship & Nature
excerpts.tangkhul_text: akui [n] head / सिर | mik [n] eye / आँख | khana [n] ear / कान | khamasung [n] nose / नाक | khamor [n] mouth / मुँह | ha [n] tooth / दाँत | pang [n] hand / हाथ | phei [n] foot / पैर | ava [n] father / पिता | aza [n] mother / माता | zingsho [n] sun / सूर्य | kachang [n] moon / चंद्रमा | tara [n] water / जल | mei [n] fire / अग्नि.
excerpts.translation_en: Nominal lexical inventory covering human anatomy with obligatory prefix a-, kinship relationships, and primary elemental entities of the physical environment.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Verbal Lexicon: Motion, Action & Cognition
excerpts.tangkhul_text: kasa [v] to do / करना | kathei [v] to see / देखना | kashā [v] to hear / सुनना | kazat [v] to walk / चलना | kapam [v] to sit / बैठना | kapi [v] to sleep / सोना | kashak [v] to eat / खाना | kapāng [v] to drink / पीना | kacham [v] to speak / बोलना. Tenses: Present -ei/-i | Past -ser/-da | Future -ra | Imperative -lu.
excerpts.translation_en: Primary verbal roots organized with infinitive prefix ka-. Tense inflection paradigms demonstrated with Subject pronouns (i, na, a).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Adjectives, Color Terms & Spatial Qualifiers
excerpts.tangkhul_text: kaphā [adj] good / अच्छा | kashi [adj] bad / बुरा | kahak [adj] big / बड़ा | kateo [adj] small / छोटा | kachon [adj] white / सफेद | muk [adj] black / काला | ngaching [adj] green / हरा | khangayei [adj] brave / वीर. Degrees of comparison: kaphā (good), kaphāmei (better), pamei (best).
excerpts.translation_en: Adjectives derived through prefixation of ka- to qualitative verbal roots. Color terminology and morphological degrees of comparison using suffix -mei.

excerpts.tangkhul_text: akha [1] / एक | khani [2] / दो | kathum [3] / तीन | mati [4] / चार | phangā [5] / पाँच | tharuk [6] / छह | shini [7] / सात | chishat [8] / आठ | chiko [9] / नौ | thakharā [10] / दस | maku [20] / बीस | shā [100] / सौ. Time: aja [today] / आज | ngalap [tomorrow] / कल | ningla [yesterday] / बीता कल.
excerpts.translation_en: Base-10 cardinal numeral system and calendar markers for day, night, month, and year.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Flora, Fauna, Agriculture & Domestic Artifacts
excerpts.tangkhul_text: si [dog] / कुत्ता | seichang [mithun] / मिथुन | hok [pig] / सूअर | vana [bird] / चिड़िया | khai [fish] / मछली | thing [tree] / पेड़ | ma [paddy] / धान | machi [salt] / नमक | haora [shawl] / शॉल | phangyai [skirt] / घाघरा | ham [pot] / मटका | tarung [post] / स्तंभ.
excerpts.translation_en: Material culture, domesticated fauna, flora, and traditional culinary items.
